ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let n>1 and let t be any real number with 0<=t<1. Set a=floor(n t). Then a<=n t<a+1, so 0<=a<=n-1. In particular, a/n is a real number in [0,1), and floor(n(a/n))=floor(a)=a.

Also, from a<=n t we get a/n<=t. Since the floor function is monotone nondecreasing on R, for each integer k with 1<=k<=n we have
floor(k a/n) <= floor(k t).
Dividing by the positive integer k preserves the inequality, so
floor(k a/n)/k <= floor(k t)/k.
Summing over k=1,2,...,n gives
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k <= sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k.

Now compute E_n at the two points. Because floor(n t)=a and floor(n(a/n))=a,
E_n(t) = a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k,
E_n(a/n) = a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k.
Using the summed inequality above, we obtain
E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).
This is exactly the claimed inequality.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with 0 <= t < 1, if a = floor(n*t), then E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).

detailed_findings.finding: Argument is logically sufficient and aligned with the stated comparison lemma.

result_payload.reason: The proof directly matches the lemma statement: define a = floor(n t), use a/n <= t, apply monotonicity of floor to each term floor(k·a/n) <= floor(k t), sum after dividing by positive k, and conclude E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n). No missing case or logical gap is apparent.
